properties.Notes: Front setback is measured from the road centerline, and a 100-foot value is used here because parcels on Route 7 are subject to a 100-foot front setback while other CON-25 parcels use 80 feet. The district also has a 500-foot minimum lot depth requirement that is not represented in the schema. Development in this district is heavily constrained by wetlands, flood hazard areas, limited service, and other environmental conditions. The bylaw permits only a studio or one-bedroom accessory dwelling unit by right; a two-bedroom ADU is conditional. The bylaw does not state a district building height maximum in CON-25.

Front setback varies by road type: parcels fronting Route 7 require a 100-foot front setback from the centerline, while parcels fronting other roads require a 25-foot front setback. A 100-foot value is used here as the maximum standardized value. The district also has a 200-foot minimum lot depth requirement that is not represented in the schema. Rear setbacks are 15 feet and side setbacks are 25 feet, but accessory structures may use reduced setbacks of 10 feet in the rear yard and 5 feet in the side yard. Multifamily parking in the bylaw is 4 spaces per 3 units and does not vary by bedroom count. Accessory dwelling units must be accessory to an owner-occupied dwelling and may not exceed 30% of the principal dwelling’s habitable floor area or 1,000 square feet, whichever is larger.

The HMU-2 district has a 100-foot front setback, 50-foot rear setback, 25-foot side setback, 200-foot frontage minimum, and 300-foot minimum lot depth. Multifamily parking in the bylaw is 4 spaces per 3 units and does not vary by bedroom count. Accessory dwelling units must be accessory to an owner-occupied dwelling and may not exceed 30% of the principal dwelling’s habitable floor area or 1,000 square feet, whichever is larger.

The IND-2 district has a standard 100-foot front setback, but parcels on Route 7 between Route 22A and the railroad tracks require a 200-foot front setback, so 200 feet is used here as the maximum standardized value. Rear setbacks are 50 feet and side setbacks are 25 feet, but both increase to 100 feet where the district abuts residential land, so 100 feet is used here as the maximum standardized value. The district also has a 300-foot minimum lot depth and a 40% lot coverage maximum. Single-family and two-family dwellings are prohibited in IND-2, so any 1F/2F dimensional fields should be treated as non-applicable rather than as actual residential allowances. Accessory dwelling units must be accessory to an owner-occupied dwelling and may not exceed 30% of the principal dwelling’s habitable floor area or 1,000 square feet, whichever is larger

Front setback is measured from the center of the road and is 100 feet. The district also has a 200-foot minimum lot depth requirement that is not represented in the schema. Accessory structures may use reduced setbacks of 10 feet in the rear yard and 5 feet in the side yard, which are not captured by the main residential setback fields. Multifamily parking in the bylaw is 4 spaces per 3 units and does not vary by bedroom count. Accessory dwelling units must be accessory to an owner-occupied dwelling and may not exceed 30% of the principal dwelling’s habitable floor area or 1,000 square feet, whichever is larger.

Front setback is measured from the road centerline. A 100-foot value is used here because parcels on Route 7 are subject to a 100-foot front setback from the centerline, while other RA-5 parcels use 80 feet. The district also requires a minimum lot depth of 450 feet and a minimum lot frontage/width of 400 feet. Multifamily parking in the bylaw is 4 spaces per 3 units and does not vary by bedroom count. Accessory dwelling units must be accessory to an owner-occupied dwelling and may not exceed 30% of the principal dwelling’s habitable floor area or 1,000 square feet, whichever is larger.

The SD-2 district has a 2-acre minimum lot size, a 200-foot frontage minimum, a 250-foot minimum lot depth, an 80-foot front setback, 25-foot rear and side setbacks, a 35-foot height maximum, and a 20% lot coverage maximum. The bylaw permits only an efficiency or one-bedroom accessory dwelling unit by right; a two-bedroom ADU is conditional. Development in this district is also affected by shoreland protection and related environmental constraints.
